title: GPU firmware, NUMA, and BMC consistency checklist for VPC/on‑prem deployments
content:
Purpose:
This note is a focused troubleshooting checklist for recurring subtle failures we see in private (VPC/on‑prem) deployments that are NOT purely software bugs. These incidents often present as intermittent model slowdowns, token latency spikes, or OOMs that manifest only after provisioning or an upgrade. The goal: fast, deterministic probes that distinguish GPU/firmware/NUMA/BMC inconsistencies from runtime or TF module issues, with clear quick mitigations and escalation cues.

Scope and when to use:
- Use when: customers report throughput regressions (sustained token/sec drop), asymmetric GPU utilization across nodes, or install/upgrade failures with cryptic CUDA errors in logs.
- This checklist is not for kernel-level development — instead for first/second responder teams (SRE, infra, solutions) to narrow hardware-layer causes quickly.

Quick hypothesis map (how problems look):
- Firmware mismatch / PCIe link flapping: intermittent huge latency spikes, dmesg with AER/PCIe link errors, device reset events.
- BMC or out-of-band flakiness: nodes become unreachable for management operations, fan/heatsink telemetry absent, IPMI timeouts while host OS is alive.
- NUMA misconfiguration: uneven CPU affinity, high cross-node memory bandwidth, some GPU processes stuck on remote memory access (higher p99 latency).
- Driver/ABI/firmware-mismatch (e.g., new kernel but older GPU FW): cuda init failures, mismatched nvidia-smi <-> driver reports, missing capabilities (MIG shapes missing).

Top-line checks (first 10 minutes)
1) Confirm customer symptoms and gather artifacts:
   - Exact timestamp(s) of incident, model id, deployment id, route, and sample request causing the regression.
   - Latest runtime logs (route/model), node syslogs (journalctl -u runtime.service), and GPU driver logs.

2) Quick health probe (low blast, non-disruptive):
   - ssh to affected node(s), run: "nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,name,uuid,driver_version,pstate,temperature.gpu,utilization.gpu,memory.total,memory.used --format=csv"
     - Expectation: all GPUs present, driver_version consistent across nodes, utilization patterns matching traffic.
   - Check kernel dmesg for recent anomalies: "dmesg --level=err,warn | tail -n 200"
     - Look for: AER/PCIe errors, GPU reset messages, UVD/dep/firmware warnings.

3) BMC/IPMI quick check (non-intrusive):
   - ipmitool -H <bmc-ip> -U <user> -P <pass> mc info; ipmitool -H <bmc-ip> -U <user> -P <pass> sdr list
     - Expectation: BMC responds quickly (<2s) and sensors present. Timeouts or error responses indicate network/OOB flakiness or bad BMC FW.

4) NUMA and CPU topology sanity:
   - lscpu; numactl --hardware; cat /proc/cmdline
     - Expectation: kernel boot parameters set per infra spec (e.g., isolcpus if used), numa nodes visible and match expected CPU sockets.
   - If GPU pinned to a CPU set, verify mapping: check runtime config for GPU<->CPU affinity and verify tasks: "ps -eo pid,psr,comm | grep runtime-worker" then "numastat -p <pid>".

In‑depth checks (next 20–40 minutes)
A) Firmware vs driver consistency
   - On each node: nvidia-smi -q | grep -E "CUDA Version|Driver Version|VBIOS Version|CUDA Capabilities" -A2
     - Cross-check driver version and VBIOS (firmware) across nodes. Small drift (one node with older VBIOS) can explain missing features (e.g., MIG shapes).
   - If using AMD/ROCm: rocminfo and /sys/class/drm/ entries.
   - Compare against golden baseline (store SHA-tagged baseline output in S3 or Confluence page).

B) PCIe and link stability probes
   - Check PCIe link width/speed: "lspci -vv -s <gpu-bdf> | grep -i 'LnkSta'". Expect negotiated width/speed consistent with HW design (e.g., x16 Gen3/Gen4).
   - dmesg for AER errors; if present, collect full AER logs and note timestamp correlation with request latency spikes.

C) Thermal/power anomalies and fan telemetry
   - nvidia-smi --query-gpu=temperature.gpu,fan.speed,power.draw --format=csv -l 1 (collect 30s)
   - Cross-check BMC sensor readouts for chassis temperature/fan speeds. Mismatches indicate BMC<->host sensor misreporting.

D) NUMA-locality stress test (non-destructive)
   - Run a short memory-locality microbenchmark pinned to the CPU socket attached to the GPU vs remote socket (e.g., "numactl --cpunodebind=0 --membind=0 ./memtest-locality") and compare bandwidth/latency. If remote reads are much slower than baseline, look for misconfigured numa_interleave or BIOS settings.

E) NVLink and inter-GPU comms (if applicable)
   - For NVLink clusters, run: nvidia-smi topo -m and NCCL tests (small NCCL allreduce) to confirm topology and latency. Mismatched topo outputs can indicate cabling or BIOS changes.

TF/Provisioning cross-checks (why TF sometimes causes hardware drift)
- Terraform may provision instances with a different machine image or instance SKU than intended (cloud flavor changes). Verify TF state: "terraform state show module.nodepool.aws_instance.foo | grep instance_type,image_id".
- Known misconfig: image bake pipeline updated kernel but not BMC/ILO firmware; node auto-reimage left old VBIOS on physical host. Add these quick checks into CI gating for images.

Mitigation steps (when you find an issue)
1) Driver/firmware mismatch (safe hotfix path):
   - If one node has older VBIOS/driver: cordon node from serving rotation (drain runtime), schedule maintenance window to update driver or firmware according to vendor instructions. Document exact vendor steps and required reboots.
2) BMC unresponsive / timeouts:
   - If only BMC affected but host OS healthy: force power cycle via cloud provider OOB or request onprem ops to perform manual power cycle. Consider reconfiguring BMC network (VLAN, MTU) if timeouts correlate to network path.
3) PCIe link flapping / AER errors:
   - Temporarily migrate workloads away from faulty GPU (if multi-GPU node) or schedule immediate maintenance. Collect PCIe logs and hardware serials for vendor RMA.
4) NUMA locality regressions:
   - Re-apply correct kernel cmdline and ensure systemd/cgroup configs match the runtime pinning policy. If misconfig happened after a kernel update, revert kernel or reconfigure cgroup cpuset.

Escalation and data to collect for hardware vendor RMA or engineering post-mortem
- Exact node identifier, serial numbers, OS image id, kernel version, driver version, VBIOS firmware hashes, BMC firmware version, ipmitool output, lspci and dmesg logs with timestamps, workload sample (trace for p99 token latency).
- Attach NCCL, nvidia-smi and numactl outputs and a short list of commands run and their outputs.

Prevention and CI additions (actionable follow-ups)
- Add a lightweight preflight that runs on every image bake and TF apply: collect nvidia-smi -q, lspci LnkSta, ipmitool mc info; compare to baseline and fail image bake if critical mismatches.
- Add gating test that simulates NUMA-sensitive benchmark and fails if cross-node memory overhead is >X% from baseline.
- Store golden hardware baselines (text blobs) per SKU in an artifacts bucket and make them easily queryable from incident runbooks.

One-page quick commands (copy-paste)
- nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,name,uuid,driver_version,pstate,temperature.gpu,utilization.gpu,memory.total,memory.used --format=csv
- dmesg --level=err,warn | tail -n 200
- ipmitool -H <bmc-ip> -U <user> -P <pass> mc info; ipmitool -H <bmc-ip> -U <user> -P <pass> sdr list
- lspci -vv -s <gpu-bdf> | grep -i 'LnkSta'
- nvidia-smi topo -m
- numactl --hardware; numastat -p <pid>

Notes and known quirks we've observed (team lore)
- Some OEMs ship GPUs with VBIOS stamped at factory that are older than cloud images expect — we saw missing MIG shapes after image bake in two separate customers.
- BMC network MTU mismatches (VLAN tagging) cause sporadic ipmitool timeouts; symptoms looked like slow host diagnostics while actual model traffic unaffected.
- Terraform image flips: a minor pipeline change swapped to a newer image repo that had a different kernel config (no NUMA balancing), which silently changed runtime behavior.

Owner and next steps
- Owner: Aisha Kapoor (eng-private-deployments).
- Short term: iterate on adding the three preflight checks to our image bake CI by end of next quarter.
- Follow-up doc: vendor-specific firmware upgrade notes per SKU (drafted, not yet published).

Appendix: useful references and vendor links
- Nvidia docs: UEFI VBIOS and driver compatibility guides (link in linked_artifacts).
- Confluence: golden baselines page (linked above).
- RFC: propose adding hardware-baseline step to Terraform module apply pipeline (RFC to be filed as INF-1459).

End of checklist.

---
Notes to responders: keep this doc as a short triage companion — expand the appendix with step-by-step vendor firmware update commands if you perform a maintenance run and we confirm RMA is needed.
